patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] proc/task_mmu: handle special PMDs in clear_refs and pagemap

version_history.subject: [PATCH] proc/task_mmu: handle special PMDs in clear_refs and pagemap

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's /proc/PID/pagemap and /proc/PID/clear_refs functionality, which causes a kernel oops when handling special PMDs (Page Map Directory Entries) that are not backed by a struct page. The fix uses vm_normal_folio_pmd() and vm_normal_page_pmd() to handle these special cases, matching the behavior of PTE paths. This patch has been tested on both broken and fixed kernels using QEMU with a test driver.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/madvise: reclaim isolated folios if PTE restart fails

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/madvise: reclaim isolated folios if PTE restart fails

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a concurrency issue in the Linux kernel's madvise functionality. When MADV_PAGEOUT is used to collect isolated folios, a concurrent operation can remove or replace the PTE table while the lock is dropped, causing pte_offset_map_lock() to return NULL and bypassing reclaim_pages(). The patch routes this failure through the existing cleanup path, ensuring that any collected folios are reclaimed or put back. This fixes a bug introduced in commit b2f557a21bc8 and resolves a reported issue.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/2] mm/mempolicy: use vm_normal_folio_pmd() in queue_folios_pmd()
series_items.patch_summary: The patch addresses a bug in the mm/mempolicy code where a VM_PFNMAP region's huge_fault installs a PMD through vmf_insert_pfn_pmd(), causing a folio to land in unpopulated vmemmap. The fix uses vm_normal_folio_pmd() instead of pmd_folio() and adds a NULL check to prevent the bad folio from carrying on into migrate_folio_add() and folio_isolate_lru().

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: LGTM (Looks Good To Me), the patch fixes a bug and looks correct.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri Sep 11, 2026 at 11:48 PM EDT, Gregory Price wrote:
> mmap a VM_PFNMAP region whose ->huge_fault installs a PMD through
> vmf_insert_pfn_pmd() - a vfio-pci MMIO BAR does this - then
>
> 	mbind(p, len, MPOL_BIND, &mask, maxnode, MPOL_MF_STRICT);
>
> With a stand-in module for the driver:
>
>   BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffff96dc0000008
>   RIP: 0010:queue_folios_pte_range+0xaf/0x440
>    walk_pgd_range+0x52b/0xaf0
>    __walk_page_range+0x6a/0x1d0
>    walk_page_range_mm_unsafe+0x193/0x230
>    queue_pages_range+0x64/0xa0
>    do_mbind+0x25e/0x640
>
> queue_folios_pmd(), inlined above, calls pmd_folio() on that PMD.  The pfn
> is raw MMIO with no memmap entry, so the folio lands in unpopulated
> vmemmap.  Neither guard stops the walk:
>
>   walk_page_test()         skips VM_PFNMAP, but queue_pages_walk_ops
>                            supplies ->test_walk, so it never runs
>   queue_pages_test_walk()  honours vma_migratable(), but only while
>                            MPOL_MF_STRICT is clear
>
> A VM_MIXEDMAP vma needs neither flag, being vma_migratable(), so plain
> mbind(MPOL_MF_MOVE) reaches this too - and there the bad folio carries on
> into migrate_folio_add() and folio_isolate_lru().  mshv_vtl_low is such a
> mapping.
>
> Use vm_normal_folio_pmd() and skip on NULL, as the PTE loop in
> queue_folios_pte_range() already does with vm_normal_folio().  On the NULL
> path, retain ACTION_CONTINUE handling for the huge zero PMD.
>
> mbind(MPOL_MF_STRICT) over a PMD mapped VM_PFNMAP region now returns 0
> rather than -EIO.  The PTE loop already returned 0 there.
>
> Fixes: 3c8e44c9b369 ("mm: mark special bits for huge pfn mappings when inject")
> Reported-by: sashiko-bot <sashiko-bot@kernel.org>
> Closes: https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260817220810.1175596-1-gourry%40gourry.net
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
> Acked-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
> ---
>  mm/mempolicy.c | 16 +++++++++-------
>  1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
>
LGTM.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/2] mm/madvise: use vm_normal_folio_pmd() in cold/pageout PMD range
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a bug in the madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range function, where it fails to validate the pfn on the way in when using vmf_insert_pfn_pmd(). The fix involves using vm_normal_folio_pmd() and skipping NULL folios, which also filters out huge zero PMDs. This patch specifically targets the cold/pageout PMD range.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Identified the bug in madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() where pfn validation is missing. Approved of the fix using vm_normal_folio_pmd().
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri Sep 11, 2026 at 11:48 PM EDT, Gregory Price wrote:
> mmap a VM_MIXEDMAP region whose ->huge_fault installs a PMD through
> vmf_insert_pfn_pmd() - mshv_vtl_low does this, and needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN
> to open - then:
>
>   madvise(p, PMD_SIZE, MADV_PAGEOUT);
>
> With a stand-in module for the driver:
>
>   BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffff587c0000008
>   RIP: 0010:madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range+0x410/0x9b0
>    walk_pgd_range+0x52b/0xaf0
>    __walk_page_range+0x6a/0x1d0
>    walk_page_range_vma_unsafe+0x8e/0x120
>    madvise_pageout+0xb2/0x180
>    madvise_vma_behavior+0x46b/0xa90
>    do_madvise+0x108/0x190
>    __x64_sys_madvise+0x26/0x30
>
> Nothing validates the pfn on the way in:
>
>   can_madv_lru_vma()     rejects VM_PFNMAP, but not VM_MIXEDMAP
>   can_fault()            *pfn = vmf->pgoff & ~(mask >> PAGE_SHIFT);
>   vmf_insert_pfn_pmd()   no pfn_valid() check
>   pmd_folio()            pfn_to_page() -> unpopulated vmemmap
>
> Even with a valid pfn the path is wrong.  The mapping carries no rmap, so
> folio_maybe_mapped_shared() sees mapcount 0, and the walker goes on to
> folio_deactivate(), or folio_isolate_lru() plus reclaim_pages(), against a
> folio this mapping does not own.
>
> Use vm_normal_folio_pmd() and skip on NULL, as the PTE half of this same
> walker already does with vm_normal_folio().  This also filters the huge
> zero PMD, so its separate check is no longer needed.
>
> Fixes: 3c8e44c9b369 ("mm: mark special bits for huge pfn mappings when inject")
> Reported-by: sashiko-bot <sashiko-bot@kernel.org>
> Closes: https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260817220810.1175596-1-gourry%40gourry.net
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v6.19+
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
> ---
>  mm/madvise.c | 7 +++----
>  1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
>
LGTM.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where special PMDs (Page Map Directory entries) are being treated as regular PMDs, leading to incorrect behavior when accessing the folio behind them. The problem arises from two page table walkers that resolve the folio using pmd_folio(), which is only valid for a PMD mapping a refcounted struct page. This patch series modifies these walkers to use vm_normal_folio() instead, ensuring consistency with the PTE halves of both walkers. As a result, mbind(MPOL_MF_STRICT) over a PMD mapped VM_PFNMAP region now returns 0 rather than -EIO.

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: The author acknowledged that there are no obvious in-tree modules reaching the special PMD state, but did not confirm or deny the existence of such modules.
review_comments.raw_body:
As far as I can tell there are no in-tree modules that reach this state,
at least not obviously.  

~Gregory

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: The author acknowledges that another issue similar to the one addressed by the patch exists in fs/proc/task_mmu.c and plans to address it, but confirms that the current patches are good to go.
review_comments.raw_body:
Ah - sashiko did report a similar issue in fs/proc/task_mmu.c though, so
I'm going to take a run at doing a larger detection run for this
problem.  These patches are good to go though.

~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/2] mm: refactor find_next_best_node to find_next_best_node_in
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the find_next_best_node function to find_next_best_node_in, which takes an explicit candidates nodemask instead of relying on N_MEMORY. This change enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates without changing any existing functionality. The new function is used in memory-tiers.c and page_alloc.c, where it replaces calls to the original function. The patch includes changes to internal.h, memory-tiers.c, and page_alloc.c, adding a new function signature and updating callers accordingly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/2] mm/page_alloc: refactor build_node_zonelist() out of build_zonelists()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code that builds zonelists in a specific order, extracting it into a new function called build_node_zonelist(). This function takes a node's ID and a list of candidate nodes as input and constructs the fallback list for that node. The original function, build_zonelists(), is simplified to call this new function for each selected node. The patch allows building zonelists from candidate nodemasks instead of just the default N_MEMORY node state list. There are no functional changes in terms of the built zonelists or their ordering.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch refactors the zonelist constructors and iterators in the Linux kernel to make them more flexible and modular. The existing behavior of picking nodes from N_MEMORY is made explicit, and a new function find_next_best_node_in() allows callers to specify the candidate set. Additionally, the per-node construction loop is extracted into a separate function build_node_zonelist(), which can be used with different candidate nodemasks and destination zonelists. These changes enable the creation of private node zonelists and improve the existing interfaces without introducing any functional changes.
